note: 8963 Liber Numeri (PL 113, cols 0379B-0446D). Eleven patches from six translation stints, consolidated 2026-09-06 and built MECHANICALLY through scripts/patch-build.mjs from data/briefs/8963-patch-sites.tsv -- never by hand. Every row resolved to exactly one site in its DECLARED column or was refused; three were refused and repaired rather than approximated.
witness_rule: Every patch here is confirmed on BOTH printings -- archive.org patrologiaecurs04migngoog (page = (col+11)/2) AND Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k5505319w (leaf f = (col+1)/2). Nothing in this file stands on one witness. See data/briefs/PL113-WITNESS-ENCODING.md: the archive copy is 1-bit JBIG2, a lossy SYMBOL-SUBSTITUTION codec, and may never be a sole witness for a letter, a digit or a point.
what_survived: Six non-words, one de-hyphenation failure, one verse digit, one wrong inflected form, one comma neither printing has, one proper name. All are OUR file against both plates. ZERO are accusations against Migne: no [sic:] and no [var:] arises from any of them, and after the patch the words are not in our Latin to carry one.
rejected_class: The two LOST HEBREW WORDS at 0427B and 0437C are NOT here and cannot be. Both plates carry them and our file has lost them, but neither witness resolves the letters securely -- the archive is 600 ppi BITONAL and Gallica is ~300 ppi, so the 1200 dpi render the stint asked for does not exist. Entering a guessed Hebrew word would be worse than the hole and invisible as an error (reference_paleography-gt-ingest). They stand as Pattern 13a clause-3 losses, marked [ed:] in the English, supplying nothing. The recoverable one (0418B) is likewise absent from this file only because it needs the same capture.

patches.why: Non-word for *cupiunt*. Both witnesses print `cupiunt` (archive p.197 600 dpi, Gallica f192). Our file only; no [sic:] is owed and after the patch the word is not in our Latin to carry one.

DE-HYPHENATION FAILURE, not a Pattern 10 split of Migne's. The plate breaks *accipiat* across a line end as `acci-` / `piat`; Corpus Corporum kept the break as a space and dropped the hyphen. Both witnesses. It wears Pattern 10's exact shape and must not be marked as one.

Digit, and made against the withdrawn verse-address class deliberately, on THREE lines, two of them outside the photographs: the archive prints an unambiguous 39 at 600 dpi, Gallica f192 agrees, and the lemma is *Septingenti* -- Nm 1:39 is Dan's 62,700 while Nm 1:59 does not exist (Numbers 1 ends at v. 54). Direction is the opposite of the withdrawn class: OUR number is wrong, not Migne's.
Real word in the wrong form -- ablative absolute *Excepto ariete* required. Both witnesses. The class Addendum A calls worthless for frequency and decisive only at the plate.

A comma NEITHER printing has (archive p.204, Gallica f199). Punctuation compared by column band, not by total. NOTE: the first two attempts at this row were REFUSED -- `qui recta, opera` spans a line break in the TEI (`qui\nrecta, opera`) and my "fix" put the escape on the wrong side of the comma. The tool refused both rather than matching something near enough.

Our file drops the `n`, leaving a singular verb under a plural subject; both witnesses print *sanctificantur*, and the Clementine Nm 18:8 agrees. English already renders the plate; no [sic:] owed, the defect is ours.
*manifestati* has no grammatical slot; Ps 50:8 reads *manifestasti*. Read at 600 dpi on the archive and at native resolution on Gallica f206. English already renders the plate.

Both witnesses print *Thabath* in the GLOSS while the VERS. 26 lemma prints *Thahath*; Migne sets both, and the English follows him at each. Only the gloss occurrence is patched -- the VERS. 26 lemma is left exactly as it stands. COLUMN CORRECTED: the stint declared 0440C and patch-build refused it, because the <pb n="0440C"/> mark falls AFTER this sentence -- the site is in 0440B. Same page (225 = cols 439/440), so the read covers it either way.
